chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khālid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, who said:

Hisham ibn Salim from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said in a long hadith of his: A man came to him and asked him, 'Is your father visited?' He said, 'Yes.' He asked, 'What is for the one who visits him?' He said, 'Paradise, if he believes in his Imamate.' He asked, 'What is for the one who leaves it, preferring to do so?' He said, 'Regret on the Day of Regret.' And he mentioned the hadith in its entirety.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam al-Husayn and the consequence of neglecting it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) distinguishes between mere physical visitation and the spiritual efficacy of *Ziyarah*, which is contingent upon affirming the Imamate of the visited figure. The text highlights the eschatological consequence of neglecting this duty out of preference (*raghba*), resulting in 'regret on the Day of Regret,' a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology regarding the separation of believers and disbelievers.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād Al-Basri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Asam, from Hishām ibn Sālim, who said:

A man came to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) and asked – as part of a longer Ḥadīth, “Should one go to the Ziyārah of your father (Ḥusain (a.s.))?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Yes.” The man asked, “What is the reward for those who go to his Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Paradise, (but only) if they believe in his Imamate.” The man asked, “What about those who neglect his Ziyārah on purpose?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “(They will) regret (it) on the Day of Regret.”
